title: The log-rank conjecture for deterministic communication
decision_reason: Source formulation, independent status corroboration, actual resolution searches and scope comparisons, full baseline screening, applied significance and separate adversarial self-review passed. Accepted draft awaits a 10–20-entry integration batch and prepublication refresh.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Total Boolean matrix M in {0,1}^{m x n}; two parties hold a row and column index
problem_fingerprint.domain: All input pairs [m] x [n], with no promise
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Universal constants C,c > 0 independent of the matrix
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: There exist C,c such that for every finite Boolean matrix a deterministic protocol satisfies the bound
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Real matrix rank; logarithms base two with 2+rank to cover ranks zero and one
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Worst-case number of communicated bits D(M)
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Deterministic interactive two-party exact communication; local computation unrestricted; no conjectural assumption

statement_source_and_scope_match: HLS §1, Conjecture 1.1 and its immediately following communication interpretation. Equivalent rectangle and cross-intersecting formulations are one problem, not additional entries. The harmless 2+rank normalization covers constant matrices.
proposed_statement_text: For each finite Boolean matrix M, two parties who know M receive respectively i and j and exchange bits until both can determine M_ij exactly. Let D(M) be the minimum worst-case communication over deterministic protocols. Do universal C,c > 0 exist with D(M) <= C [log_2(2+rank_R M)]^c for all M?
applied_significance: Two processors holding separate inputs must compute a prescribed Boolean decision exactly. The conjecture asks whether the real linear-algebraic complexity of its truth table universally controls the required interaction, up to a fixed power of a logarithm; local computation is unrestricted.

source_records.title: The Log-Rank Conjecture: New Equivalent Formulations
source_records.supported_claim: Explicitly leaves log-rank open. Signed rectangle rank approximates real rank, but positivity conversion remains conjectural.

source_records.title: Matrix discrepancy and the log-rank conjecture
source_records.supported_claim: General bound O(sqrt(r)); conjectural target remains polylogarithmic.
source_records.arxiv_version_history: 2311.18524: v1 2023-11-30 only; journal version inspected separately

source_records.title: Alphabet-Preserving Lifting for the Log-Rank Conjecture
source_records.supported_claim: Provides an explicit lower-bound construction still compatible with a fixed polylogarithmic upper bound; not asserted here to be the strongest known lower bound among all constructions.

source_records.title: The Log-Approximate-Rank Conjecture is False
source_records.supported_claim: Separates randomized bounded-error communication from approximate rank, not deterministic communication from exact real rank.

source_records.title: Refuting approaches to the log-rank conjecture for XOR functions
source_records.supported_claim: Refutes auxiliary Fourier-support assertions; §5 explicitly explains why its functions do not refute log-rank.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: No baseline entry asks this universal relation between exact communication and real rank. Equivalent rectangle/XOR reformulations are not separate entries.

open_status_evidence_summary: HLS v3 (August 2026) explicitly formulates the unresolved conjecture; independent ST gives a square-root-rank bound. Located apparent refutations concern approximate rank or proposed proof methods; the recent lower bound does not exceed every fixed polylogarithm.
independent_status_corroboration: ST independently formulates the problem and supplies only a square-root-rank upper bound; HLS reaffirms the gap in August 2026.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: ST proves D(M)=O(sqrt(rank_R M)); this does not give any fixed power of log rank.

issues_found: Both-party output differs by at most one final bit from standard one-party output; fixed constants absorb it.
Real exact rank and total deterministic communication preserved.
Auxiliary Fourier refutation and randomized approximate-rank disproof do not settle this statement.
No arbitrary split into equivalent formulations.
